item.title: Escambia County Meets FEMA Public Assistance Threshold; Individual Assistance Still Pending
item.dc:creator: news6334
item.description: PENSACOLA, Fla. — Escambia County has reached an important milestone in its effort to secure federal assistance following Hurricane Isaias. County officials announced Wednesday that joint damage-assessment teams have determined Escambia meets the threshold for FEMA Public Assistance. That program provides reimbursement for eligible government…
item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — Escambia County has reached an important milestone in its effort to secure federal assistance following Hurricane Isaias.


County officials announced Wednesday that joint damage-assessment teams have determined Escambia meets the threshold for FEMA Public Assistance.


That program provides reimbursement for eligible government expenses associated with disaster response and recovery.


Those expenses can include debris removal, emergency protective measures and repairs to damaged public infrastructure.


However, the county's announcement does not mean federal assistance has been approved for individual homeowners.


FEMA Individual Assistance is a separate program that can provide eligible households with assistance for disaster-related needs.


County officials said Wednesday evening that assessment teams were continuing to document residential damage throughout Escambia County and the City of Pensacola.

Once the assessments are complete, the information will be forwarded to the state to support a request for a presidential major disaster declaration.


Both Public Assistance and Individual Assistance require the appropriate federal declaration before funding can move forward.


Escambia County previously estimated approximately $64 million in public damage and recovery costs following Hurricane Isaias.


Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves also reported that more than $70 million in private-property damage had been documented within the city as of Tuesday evening.


Those figures represent different categories of damage and should not be confused with approved federal reimbursement amounts.

County officials are encouraging residents to continue reporting hurricane damage through the county's official damage-reporting system.


Reporting damage helps document the community's losses but is not the same as applying for FEMA assistance.

item.title: Pensacola Police Mourn Detective Angela Nieto Following Fatal Motorcycle Crash
item.dc:creator: news6334

item.content:encoded:
PENSACOLA, Fla. — The Pensacola Police Department is mourning the death of Detective Angela Nieto, who was killed Wednesday night in an off-duty motorcycle crash on the Barrancas Avenue bridge over Bayou Chico.


The crash happened around 8 p.m. October 14.


According to Pensacola Police, Nieto was a passenger on a motorcycle being operated by a male friend. The motorcycle was traveling eastbound when the driver lost control while negotiating a curve.


Nieto died at the scene. The motorcycle's driver was transported to a local hospital with injuries described as non-life-threatening.


During an interview Thursday morning on NewsRadio 92.3's Pensacola's Morning News, department spokesman Mike Wood described the loss as devastating for Nieto's family and fellow officers.


Wood said Nieto joined Pensacola Police as a cadet in January 2019 and became a sworn officer that July.


Before joining the department, she served in the military. Wood also described Nieto as a mother of two.


"She was one to serve," Wood said during the interview. "And I also want to say that she's a mother of two. So yeah, we're missing a good one here."


Wood said the department's Honor Guard responded Wednesday night, and law enforcement officers from several agencies participated in a procession following the crash.

The department is working to support Nieto's family and colleagues as funeral arrangements are made.


Pensacola Police and the Florida Highway Patrol are investigating the crash.


Authorities have not announced a determination of its cause.

item.title: SailGP launches North American training base in Pensacola
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: High-speed sailing competition SailGP is officially opening its North American training base in Pensacola on Monday, according to a media advisory from the organization. The facility, located at American Magic's High Performance Center at the Port of Pensacola, will serve as a year-round training hub for SailGP teams competing in the Rolex SailGP…
item.content:encoded:
High-speed sailing competition SailGP is officially opening its North American training base in Pensacola on Monday, according to a media advisory from the organization.

The facility, located at American Magic's High Performance Center at the Port of Pensacola, will serve as a year-round training hub for SailGP teams competing in the Rolex SailGP Championship. Teams pilot identical 50-foot foiling catamarans that race at speeds exceeding 60 miles per hour. Pensacola was selected for its world-class sailing facilities, consistent wind conditions, and central U.S. location. The agreement runs for six seasons, with teams beginning training in October 2026.

The official launch event is scheduled for Monday, October 19 at 9:30 a.m. at the American Magic High Performance Center (Warehouse 10) in the Port of Pensacola. SailGP executives, Pensacola Mayor D.C. Reeves, and athletes from the Emirates GBR SailGP Team — the 2025 Rolex SailGP Champions — will participate. Media are invited for behind-the-scenes tours and athlete interviews. Government-issued ID is required for facility access.

item.content:encoded:
North Escambia will enjoy another warm day Thursday with sunny skies and a high near 88 degrees, according to the National Weather Service forecast. Winds will remain light, with an easterly breeze around 5 mph.

Thursday night clouds increase as temperatures drop to around 64 degrees. Friday starts mostly cloudy through mid-morning before clearing to sunny skies, with a high near 86 degrees—still warm but slightly cooler than Thursday.

The pattern shifts over the weekend, with meteorologists calling for windier conditions and cooler temperatures moving in, so residents should prepare for more active weather ahead.

item.content:encoded:
An off-duty Pensacola Police Department detective died Wednesday night in a motorcycle crash on the Barrancas Bridge. Detective Angela Nieto was fatally injured in the wreck, which occurred around 8:00 p.m. on October 14, according to Pensacola Police Department Public Information Officer Mike Wood.

The crash marks a significant loss for the Pensacola Police Department. Nieto's death comes as the agency and the broader Pensacola community process the tragedy.

The Pensacola Police Department has not yet released additional details about the circumstances surrounding the crash or whether other vehicles were involved. Authorities are continuing to investigate the incident.

item.content:encoded:

The Santa Rosa County health department provides a range of public health services to the community. No additional details about the nature or extent of the weather damage were provided in the reopening notice.

Century is one of several communities across Northwest Florida dealing with similar post-storm challenges, including power outages and infrastructure damage.

item.title: ECAT Adjusts Routes Thursday Due to Storm Debris
item.dc:creator: newsroom

ECAT will run standard service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit available from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not operate at all Thursday.…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Area Transit will resume normal operating hours Thursday, Oct. 15, but several routes will see modifications due to debris and road conditions left behind from recent weather.

ECAT will run standard service from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., with FlexTransit available from 5 a.m. to 8 p.m. However, Route 48 will not operate at all Thursday. Routes 45 North and 51 will skip service on Briese Lane and Ensley Street respectively, with riders directed to alternative pickup locations on Johnson Avenue and Cody Road.

The University of West Florida trolleys also will not run Thursday. ECAT warns that delays remain possible across the system due to ongoing debris on roadways, and riders should plan for extra travel time. For specifics on your route, call ECAT at 850-595-3228.

item.title: DeSantis Reappoints Clark, Passidomo-Smith to Florida Public Service Commission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Governor Ron DeSantis announced Wednesday the reappointment of Gary Clark and Gabriella Passidomo-Smith to the Florida Public Service Commission, a regulatory body that oversees the state's utility companies. Clark, of Chipley, has served as a PSC Commissioner since 2017. Before that role, he worked as Deputy Secretary of Land and Recreation for…
item.content:encoded:
Governor Ron DeSantis announced Wednesday the reappointment of Gary Clark and Gabriella Passidomo-Smith to the Florida Public Service Commission, a regulatory body that oversees the state's utility companies.

Clark, of Chipley, has served as a PSC Commissioner since 2017. Before that role, he worked as Deputy Secretary of Land and Recreation for the Florida Department of Environmental Protection and served on the Washington County School Board, Chipola College District Board of Trustees, and the Northwest Florida Water Management District Governing Board. He holds a bachelor's degree in business administration from the University of Phoenix.

Passidomo-Smith, based in Tallahassee, has been a PSC Commissioner since 2021. She previously worked as an attorney in the Regulatory Analysis Section of the PSC's Office of the General Counsel and sits on committees within the National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners focused on gas utility regulation and pipeline safety. She earned her bachelor's degree in political science from the University of Florida and a juris doctor from Washington and Lee University School of Law.

Both appointments are subject to confirmation by the Florida Senate.

item.title: Navarre Beach lifts boil water notice after safety testing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Santa Rosa County has rescinded a boil water notice for all Navarre Beach Utilities customers after bacteriological testing confirmed the water is safe to drink, according to a county announcement Wednesday afternoon. The notice, which had required customers to boil water before consumption, was lifted following completion of required safety…
item.content:encoded:
Santa Rosa County has rescinded a boil water notice for all Navarre Beach Utilities customers after bacteriological testing confirmed the water is safe to drink, according to a county announcement Wednesday afternoon.

The notice, which had required customers to boil water before consumption, was lifted following completion of required safety surveys. Santa Rosa County did not specify how long the notice had been in effect or what prompted the initial precaution.

Other water utilities in Santa Rosa County remain under boil water notices, including the City of Milton Water, Town of Jay, Bagdad, and Garcon Point Water. Customers of those systems should continue to boil water until further notice from the county.
